title: Quant passthrough cascade scheduler for attention to reduce dequant overhead
creator: Alicia Mendoza
description: Problem: dequant/copy overhead dominates tail latency for streaming decode on INT8/FP8 model paths when attention prefill and decode alternate frequently. Current kernel selection frequently inserts eager dequant and memory copies between prefill and decode stages, which inflates per-token CPU/GPU overhead and reduces batching headroom. Goal: design and implement a scheduler + small kernel ABI changes that allow quantized attention kernels to 'passthrough' quantized buffers across prefill->decode boundaries when safe, falling back to selective dequant only when downstream ops or incompatible model layers require it.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end streaming decode p95 latency reduced by >= 12% on INT8 paths compared to current baseline for 1-4 token incremental decodes
Per-request GPU memory copies due to dequant reduced by >= 30% in representative chat workload trace
No correctness regressions on canonical tokenization and logits outputs across the certified model matrix (acceptance test suite)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and default-off for Dedicated/Private beta; canary rollout plan documented
design_notes: Introduce a lightweight kernel ABI hint (quant_passthrough=bool, required_alignment=int) that signals kernels can consume and produce quantized tensors without forcing float32 epilogues.
Scheduler maintains a short-lived 'quant lineage' annotation per request that tracks compatible quant formats (INT8/FP8/scale metadata) and whether KV caches are safe to keep in quantized form.

Two-stage strategy: 1) Path discovery during prefill to mark layers compatible with passthrough; 2) In decode, prefer passthrough kernels and only run per-layer dequant when model-layer ABI mismatches are detected.
Fallback: conservative per-layer whitelist; on mismatch, run existing dequant kernel and evict quant lineage for remainder of request.
Compatibility: interacts with batching and KV cache merging; must preserve correctness for multi-tenant Dedicated pools and avoid cross-request contamination.
implementation_plan: Spike: implement prototype kernel ABI changes and tiny shim for linearized attention kernel to accept quant buffers (1 week). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287
Scheduler: add quant-lineage annotations at request dispatch and extend prefill pass to populate compatibility map (2 weeks).
KV cache: modify KV write path to optionally write quant-formatted cache and add read-time upcast for incompatible consumer kernels (1 week).
Testing harness: add microbench harness for 1-8 token incremental decodes with trace replays and a synthetic adversarial model that flips precision mid-model (3 days).
Canary rollout: feature flag behind runtime-opt.quanta_passthrough; run internally on low-traffic sandbox then 5% production canary for a week with alerting pins (1 week).
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel ABI: ensure kernels can indicate passthrough capability and fail gracefully when passed wrong metadata.
Integration tests: prefill->decode streaming scenarios across 6 certified models (small/medium/large families) to validate outputs match golden traces.
Performance tests: run our scaled tracebench workload (chat-realtime) comparing token throughput, p50/p95 latencies, and GPU memcpy counts between baseline and passthrough enabled.
Fuzz: randomize layer precision flips to ensure safe fallback paths trigger and do not corrupt KV caches.
Canary monitoring: add SLO dashboards for per-route latency, dequant memcpy bytes, and error rates; automatic rollback if error spike or >2% output divergence.
Security review: ensure quant metadata does not leak cross-tenant information (audit with Security team).
performance_benchmarks: Baseline (INT8 path, current runtime): 1-token incremental decode p95 = 64ms; memcpy per-request = 12MB; tokens/sec (single-stream) = 180
Target (passthrough enabled): expected p95 = <=56ms (-12.5%); memcpy per-request <=8MB (-33%); tokens/sec >=210 (+16.7%)
Measured prototype (synthetic medium model): p95 = 54ms (-15.6%); memcpy = 7.6MB (-36.7%); tokens/sec = 224 (+24.4%). Note: prototype runs without full batching interactions; final numbers may vary.
risks: Incorrect lineage propagation can corrupt KV cache semantics across requests — mitigation: lineage is request-scoped and validated against per-layer checksums.
Some vendor kernels (third-party GPU libs) may not support quant passthrough; mitigation: provider adapters and fallback to dequant path.
Complexity in interop with autoscaling and Dedicated pools — mitigation: default-off in Dedicated until validated, conservative rollout.
Potential slight accuracy drift if quant metadata handling differs between kernels; mitigation: regression tests and optional auto-requantization step before logits if drift detected.
